extracted.intended_audience: federal policymakers, science agency leaders, university research administrators, and science-policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A set of national-level recommendations and evaluative principles for organizing, funding, and governing basic scientific research, training scientific talent, publication policy, and agency design (the report that led to creation of NSF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: Government should extend financial support to basic scientific research in universities, colleges, and research institutes because basic research is the source of new scientific knowledge essential to medicine, national security, new industries, and jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic research is described as 'scientific capital' and a long-term process; it produces the underlying knowledge from which new products and industries arise and must be funded so that discovery potential is sustained rather than expecting immediate applied results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review as the principal selection mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding decisions should be based on a commitment to merit review, a process that discerns the most promising research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merit review is characterized as a hallmark of value—generating a vast array of research designs that produce remarkable discoveries (NSF's history cited as supporting this). The report links merit review to national impact and to the identification of promising work across disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal and development of scientific talent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government should implement programs to discover and develop scientific talent (scholarships, fellowships, training) so that 'every boy and girl shall know that, if he shows that he has what it takes, the sky is the limit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include nationwide selection processes, inventories of activities/interests, application and recommendation forms, state and national selection committees, timelines for selection and acceptance, and dedicated funding; the report emphasizes research into selection methods and adequate funds for that research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of inquiry and prompt publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom of inquiry must be preserved and wartime security restrictions on scientific information should be lifted promptly so the frontiers of science can be 'thrown open.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report argues that broad dissemination is better for national security long-term and that publication should be allowed as soon as information cannot be turned against the nation in the present war. Publication should be encouraged and facilitated for both government and contractor scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board to control release and promote publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish within the National Academy of Sciences a standing board to control the release of formerly classified scientific information and to promote its publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board should be adequately staffed, include joint Army, Navy, and civilian membership, adopt a liberal release policy, act promptly, coordinate release with allies where material is jointly held, encourage scientists to publish, stimulate administrative support for publication, and ensure adequate financing for publication and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Five Fundamentals for a new science agency
rubrics_metrics.description: A new agency should be founded on 'The Five Fundamentals' including: stability and continuity of funding; administration of grants by citizens with deep understanding of scientific research and education; refrain from operating laboratories of its own; control of the grant environment by universities and research institutes; and accountability to the President and Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fundamentals guide organizational design and governance (the report notes some eventual differences in practice but asserts these as core principles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency should not operate its own laboratories
rubrics_metrics.description: The funding agency should refrain from operating laboratories of its own and instead leave direct research operation to universities and research institutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to preserve the grant environment and avoid agency-owned labs dominating the research agenda; it is one of the Five Fundamentals for agency design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of the grant environment by universities and research institutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant environment (management and conduct of research) should be controlled by universities and research institutes rather than by the funding agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves academic freedom and the environment 'most conducive to the creation of new scientific knowledge' and reduces pressure for immediate applied results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and continuity of funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Research funding should be stable and continuous to support long-term basic research rather than short-term, immediate-result-driven funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic research 'ceases to be basic if immediate results are expected on short-term support'; the report stresses long-term commitments as essential to discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration of grants by scientifically knowledgeable citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants and awards should be administered by citizens who have deep understanding of scientific research and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert, peer-based administration ensures informed decisions about research and training investments; part of agency governance fundamentals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability to the President and Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: The new agency must be accountable to the President and to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains democratic oversight while preserving scientific leadership in program decisions; listed among the Five Fundamentals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government support for basic medical research in academic medical schools
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government should extend financial support to basic medical research in medical schools and universities because traditional private funding is insufficient and research costs are rising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that medical/basic biomedical research responsibility 'falls primarily upon the medical schools and universities' but needs government support to maintain progress in medicine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilian-controlled military-relevant research with congressional funding
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be civilian-controlled organizations (with close liaison to the Army and Navy) that receive funds directly from Congress and have clear powers to initiate military research to supplement service-controlled research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuation of civilian scientist contributions to national security in peacetime while preserving civilian oversight and direct congressional funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between basic research and programs aimed at technology transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: While the agency's primary role is supporting basic research, it may fund programs designed to speed technology transfer and practical outcomes (e.g., Engineering Research Centers, Innovation Corps) when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes the original separation envisioned (basic research by government/academia, applied by industry) but accepts funding of some applied/transfer-oriented programs to achieve public benefit and respond to changing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for centers of basic research (colleges, universities, research institutes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen centers of basic research—colleges, universities, and research institutes—as the principal places for expanding frontiers of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These institutions provide environments least under pressure for immediate results; government should concentrate support there rather than operate large in-house labs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for education and human resources across all levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Support research and programs that improve STEM education from primary through graduate levels and informal learning, and develop a skilled technical workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally focused on graduate fellowships, the recommended portfolio includes K–12, undergraduate, graduate, and informal learning; partnerships with academe, industry, nonprofits, and other agencies are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broaden participation and geographic distribution of research funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage broader participation in science (women, underrepresented minorities, diverse career paths) and address concentration of funding geographically (e.g., EPSCoR) so opportunity is not limited by identity or location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs like INCLUDES and EPSCoR (Experimental/Established Program to Stimulate Competitive Research) are cited as mechanisms to scale up inclusion and build institutional capacity nationwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage interdisciplinary 'convergence' and inclusion of social sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote collaboration across directorates and disciplines (convergence) recognizing that many urgent issues require multidisciplinary approaches; include social sciences as part of the research enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report documents creation and evolution of social sciences within the foundation and stresses their relevance to national decision-making and quality of life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in large shared facilities and advanced computational infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund large-scale facilities and computational resources (e.g., continental-scale observatories, supercomputers) that enable discovery across disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include the National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON), high-performance computing, and facilities that enable new research designs and discovery potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote international exchange and coordination on release/publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government should actively promote the international flow of scientific information and coordinate release decisions with allied countries when information is jointly held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad dissemination fosters competitiveness and scientific progress; a central board should handle international coordination to minimize friction and delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication decision criteria and financing
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions about publishing government-financed research should be made on the basis of public interest in dissemination, not on the presence or absence of funds to defray publication and distribution costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee recommends provision of adequate financing for publication and distribution and encourages preparation of manuscripts while research teams are still assembled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative encouragement of prompt publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative officers of cognizant government agencies should actively assist and stimulate prompt publication by government scientists and contractors once security restrictions are relaxed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'courageous policy' by agency administrators will reduce delays; the timing for manuscript preparation may be at the close of contracts when teams and records are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process for scholarship programs and research into selection methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a multi-stage, nationwide selection process for scholarships (screening large applicant pools, state committees, national office coordination, timelines for notification and acceptance) and allocate funds for research to improve selection methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report details schedules (application deadlines, state committee reviews, public announcements), estimated costs for screening and selection, and emphasizes that adequate funds for research on selection methods are a long-run economy and essential for effective candidate identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lift security restrictions promptly and uniformly
rubrics_metrics.description: Release scientific material from military classification as soon as conditions permit, and avoid unfair situations where information is released in one place but restricted in another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform lifting prevents morale issues among scientists; release should generally occur when information cannot be used against the nation in the current war and should avoid divulging embodiments in actual military devices where sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of returning servicemen education and Army universities
rubrics_metrics.description: Make wartime-developed techniques and up-to-date scientific knowledge available in Army universities overseas so returning servicemen can resume scientific training with current advances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of material and selection of instructors familiar with latest developments will prevent training postwar cohorts on outdated (e.g., 1940-era) knowledge and help narrow wartime deficits in scientists and engineers.
